category_fits.label: Technology & Innovation
category_fits.why_fit: The report examines technology innovations and shifts, including digital assistants spreading across devices and VR/AR developing into a computing platform.
category_fits.why_not_fit: The outlook also covers media markets and revenue forecasts, so it is broader than technology alone.
evidence_sections: Smart Speaker Battles are about the Great Digital Assistant Wars
Reality Computing: VR/AR Move from Entertainment to the Next Big Computing Platform
supported_topic_rules: Evidence repeatedly discusses infrastructure, enterprise technology, robotics, cybersecurity, hardware, or major technology shifts.
Technology change is the report main lens rather than a supporting enabler for another category.
The report is primarily about immersive experiences, spatial computing, virtual worlds, or Metaverse technology.
rule_evidence_sections: Smart Speaker Battles are about the Great Digital Assistant Wars
Reality Computing: VR/AR Move from Entertainment to the Next Big Computing Platform
centrality_evidence_sections: Smart Speaker Battles are about the Great Digital Assistant Wars
Reality Computing: VR/AR Move from Entertainment to the Next Big Computing Platform

category_fits.label: Business Performance & Growth
category_fits.why_fit: The opening analysis forecasts $302B in global consumer Internet and media revenue growth and compares growth rates across revenue segments.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Revenue forecasts are a major component, but the report also centrally examines technology, consumer use, and media formats rather than focusing only on business performance.
evidence_sections: $300 Billion in Tech and Media Growth Dollars
supported_topic_rules: Evidence repeatedly emphasizes growth, revenue, margin, productivity, performance ranking, or strategic business levers.
The report is meant to guide business performance decisions, not just describe category trends.
rule_evidence_sections: $300 Billion in Tech and Media Growth Dollars
centrality_evidence_sections: $300 Billion in Tech and Media Growth Dollars

category_fits.label: Social, Short Video & Creator
category_fits.why_fit: A dedicated section analyzes creator concentration on YouTube and the split of top-creator views between influencers and media companies across platforms.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Creator and social-video dynamics are one substantial subject among many in the broader tech and media outlook, not its dominant focus.
evidence_sections: Big Influencers and Media Brands will Rule Web Video
supported_topic_rules: Evidence repeatedly focuses on creators, creator economics, short-form video, social platform behavior, or community-driven content strategy.
rule_evidence_sections: Big Influencers and Media Brands will Rule Web Video
centrality_evidence_sections: Big Influencers and Media Brands will Rule Web Video

category_fits.label: Streaming & Connected TV
category_fits.why_fit: The report includes premium video and Virtual Pay TV/SVOD churn analysis, alongside broader video-market coverage.
category_fits.why_not_fit: The context does not establish streaming or television-like video as the report's dominant subject; it also devotes attention to web-video creators, technology, and other media topics.
evidence_sections: Big Influencers and Media Brands will Rule Web Video
rejected_topic_rules: Reject when streaming is just one channel benchmark inside a broader media report.
rule_evidence_sections: Big Influencers and Media Brands will Rule Web Video

category_fits.label: Consumer Behavior & Insights
category_fits.why_fit: The report uses U.S. consumer research and forecasts daily technology and media use, including the role of smart speakers in audio and video consumption.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Consumer measures support a broader technology and media outlook; the report is not primarily about consumer attitudes or behavior as an independent subject.
evidence_sections: There are 31 Hours in a Day
Smart Speaker Battles are about the Great Digital Assistant Wars
rejected_topic_rules: Reject when consumer metrics are just supporting evidence inside a brand, media, or financial performance report.
rule_evidence_sections: There are 31 Hours in a Day

category_fits.label: Advertising Strategy & Media
category_fits.why_fit: Advertising revenue is one of the report's global market segments, and it discusses media brands and web-video platforms.
category_fits.why_not_fit: The context does not describe media planning, buying, advertising effectiveness, or investment guidance as a central focus; advertising appears as one part of a wider market outlook.
evidence_sections: $300 Billion in Tech and Media Growth Dollars
Big Influencers and Media Brands will Rule Web Video
rejected_topic_rules: Reject when media appears only as one route inside a broader consumer or business trends report.
